claim: A holographic force signal (power-law scaling F(dr) ~ dr^{-alpha} with alpha in [3.5, 4.5]) is detectable above NISQ noise in a trapped-ion MERA experiment at the scale demonstrated by Miao et al. (2412.18602), provided that two-qubit gate fidelity exceeds 99.5% and the system size is at least 8 qubits. Specifically: the Barthel group's experiment achieved log-law entanglement entropy at criticality on trapped-ion hardware with a depth-4 MERA circuit. Our force measurement requires computing hologron energy differences at 4-8 boundary separations dr=1..8. The signal-to-noise ratio for the force measurement scales as (F_signal / noise_floor) where noise_floor ~ 1 - F_2Q^{N_gates}, and for our 8q chi=3 MERA the energy error at perfect gates is 0.00% (SIM-2026-015). Therefore: at 99.5% two-qubit fidelity with N_gates ~ 40 two-qubit gates (chi=3, 8q), the cumulative noise floor is approximately 1 - 0.995^40 ~ 18%, which is above the force signal amplitude at dr=6..8 but below the signal at dr=1..3. We predict force-law detection at short separations (dr=1..4) is feasible at current Helios fidelity (99.921%), while long-range separations (dr>6) require fault-tolerant noise levels.
confidence_rationale: Miao et al. 2412.18602 directly demonstrates MERA on trapped-ion hardware at criticality, providing empirical validation of the circuit compilation approach. Our 0.00% energy error at 8q chi=3 (SIM-2026-015) establishes the ideal-case baseline. The gate-count and noise propagation estimate is standard circuit noise modeling. Confidence is medium (not high) because: (1) we have not explicitly computed N_gates for our specific chi=3 force-measurement circuit (vs Miao's entanglement-only circuit); (2) cross-talk and coherent errors may dominate over incoherent gate errors at Helios scale; (3) the force measurement requires subtracting two energy values, so systematic errors partially cancel but statistical noise adds in quadrature.
test_design: 1. Count two-qubit gate depth in our chi=3 8q MERA ansatz (already coded for SIM-2026-015). 2. Apply Helios noise model: depolarizing error rate p = 1 - 0.99921 = 0.00079 per two-qubit gate. Compute cumulative fidelity F_total = (1-p)^{N_2Q}. 3. Simulate force measurement under this noise model using Qiskit Aer (depolarizing channel). Extract hologron energy at dr=1..8 with 10,000 shots. Compare to noiseless SIM-2026-015 values. 4. Identify the maximum dr at which the force signal remains above 3-sigma noise floor. 5. If dr_max >= 4, the Helios run is predicted to detect the alpha~4 force law (4 points span 2 orders of magnitude in r, sufficient for a power-law fit). Refine estimate using Miao et al.'s actual compiled gate count as a calibration reference.
refutation_criteria: If noise-model simulation shows force signal falls below 3-sigma at dr >= 2 (i.e., only 1 clean data point), the Helios run cannot detect a power law and the hypothesis is refuted. If Miao et al.'s actual compiled circuit has > 200 two-qubit gates for an 8q MERA (implying our circuit would be similarly deep), the 99.921% fidelity gate is insufficient and the hypothesis is refuted.
hardware_required: Local simulation (Qiskit Aer noise model, CPU) for feasibility check. Quantinuum Helios 57-94q for experimental validation.
feasibility_notes: Noise-model simulation (Qiskit Aer, depolarizing channel) is local CPU, no new hardware access needed. Helios access already proposed via QCUP PHY204. Gate count for chi=3 8q circuit must be verified from SIM-2026-015 ansatz code — this is the one unverified assumption. Math checks: (1-0.00079)^40 ~ 0.969, leaving 3.1% cumulative error — force signal at dr=1..3 is ~100x above this floor, dr=4..6 is 10-30x above. TESTABLE_NOW via simulation; Helios experimental run is TESTABLE_NOW pending QCUP resubmission approval.
philosophical_implications: If the gate-fidelity threshold is confirmed (force signal detectable at Helios 99.921% for dr=1..4), it establishes a precise boundary between the quantum and classical regimes of holographic geometry: below the fidelity threshold, the emergent bulk geometry is unresolvable through decoherence noise; above it, geometry becomes an experimentally accessible fact. This resonates with relational quantum mechanics (Rovelli): physical quantities, including bulk geometry, only have meaning relative to an observer's measurement capacity. The fidelity threshold is the minimum 'observer quality' required for the holographic dictionary to be physically meaningful in the laboratory. In eternalism (the block universe), the holographic bulk geometry exists timelessly; what the fidelity threshold specifies is not whether the geometry exists, but whether a particular physical process (our MERA circuit) can serve as a faithful map from the boundary to that pre-existing geometry. The Barthel group's experimental precedent (PAPER-2026-043) grounds this in laboratory reality rather than pure speculation.

status_writeback_2026_08_17.verified_against: SIM-2026-019.json field verdict reads PARTIALLY_REFUTED verbatim (Helios fidelity threshold noise-model analysis for the chi=3 8q MERA, status COMPLETE). The status written here is that record's own verdict.
status_writeback_2026_08_17.what_was_refuted: The hypothesis's stated 99.5% two-qubit-fidelity threshold. The project's own record concludes Helios is insufficient for power-law DETECTION at the claimed range; the required fidelity is ~99.99%, not 99.5%.
status_writeback_2026_08_17.what_survives: Force-EXISTENCE at short separation (dr = 1..2) remains viable at the Helios frontier. That is why the verdict is PARTIALLY_REFUTED and not REFUTED.
status_writeback_2026_08_17.disclosure_note: The audit (defect D-14c) records that this PARTIALLY_REFUTED verdict appears nowhere in the submitted manuscript's hardware section. Writing it into this record does not discharge that; the manuscript is outside this pass's ownership and the omission is reported, not fixed.
